findings.title: New `related_finding_ids` field uses `.optional()` instead of `.nullish()`
findings.rationale: Rule 1 of the api-contract-house-rules states that fields in `Review` and `Finding` must use `.nullish()`, not `.optional()`. The new `related_finding_ids` field is added with `.optional()`, which under strict mode makes it a required property for the reviewer model, forcing it to produce a value on every finding. The correct pattern, as shown in the rule, is `.nullish()` to allow `null`. This is a warning-level issue because the only symptom is a console warning, not a functional break.

findings.title: New `Finding` field uses `.optional()` instead of `.nullish()`
findings.rationale: The new `related_finding_ids` field is added to the `Finding` schema with `.optional()`. Per house rule 1, fields in `Review` and `Finding` must use `.nullish()` because these schemas are sent with `strict: true`, which lists every property as required. With `.optional()`, the reviewer model must produce a value for this field on every finding and will invent one, causing a console warning. The repo convention (e.g., `suggestion: z.string().nullish()` at line 56) uses `.nullish()` for this reason. The same issue exists in the client copy at `client/src/vendor/shared/contracts/findings.ts:63`.

findings.title: Client refresh call bypasses ApiError contract
findings.rationale: The new refresh button calls `api.post<PrDetail>("/pulls/${prId}/refresh")`. The house rule requires that any client call to the engine that can return a non-2xx response must throw `ApiError` (or return the error body as data). The `api.post` helper is a direct `fetch` wrapper that, on a non-2xx response, throws a plain `Error` with the status text, not an `ApiError`. This means the page's error handling (which checks `error instanceof ApiError`) will not catch the refresh failure, and the user will see a generic error message and lose the server's error code and message. This is a regression from the existing pattern where all other client calls go through `api.ts` and surface `ApiError`.

findings.title: Shared contract copies not updated together
findings.rationale: The new `POST /pulls/:id/refresh` route is added to the server, but the corresponding client-side contract (in `client/src/vendor/shared/`) is not updated in this diff. The house rule states that a change to one copy of a shared contract must be mirrored in the other copy in the same diff. The server now exposes a new endpoint that the client will call, but the client's contract file does not know about it. This is a warning because the client will still work (it calls the endpoint directly), but the two copies are now out of sync, and any future change to the contract could silently break the client.

findings.title: PR list backfill removed
findings.rationale: The diff removes the backfill of `filesCount` and `commitsCount` on the PR list (the `files_count` and `commits_count` fields) that was previously done during the detail fetch. Now that the detail fetch is a pure read, the list view will no longer get the real file/commit counts from GitHub. This is a behavior change for the Pull Requests list page, which previously showed real sizes. The list will now show stale or zero counts until a refresh is explicitly triggered. This is a warning because the list still works, but the data it shows is no longer fresh.

findings.title: GET /pulls/:id no longer returns the full PrDetail; files/commits are now empty until a refresh
findings.rationale: The GET handler previously fetched the live detail from GitHub and returned a complete PrDetail (files, commits, files_count, etc.). The diff removes that fetch and returns a partial object built only from the stored pull request row. Any caller that reads .files, .commits, .files_count, or .commits_count from the GET response now gets empty/undefined values. The client's own PrDetailHeader and the Pull Requests list (which reads filesCount) are affected. The compatible alternative is to keep the GET response shape stable by returning the stored detail (which the refresh endpoint persists) and only add the new POST /pulls/:id/refresh for explicit freshness. If the stored detail is not yet available, return the partial object but document that files/commits are best-effort and require a refresh.

findings.title: New POST /pulls/:id/refresh is not validated against the shared PrDetail schema; a malformed GitHub payload produces a 500 instead of a 422
findings.rationale: The new refresh route returns the raw detail from gh.getPullRequest without validating it against the shared PrDetail schema. The old GET handler validated the response through the route's response schema. If GitHub returns a field with the wrong type (e.g. files_count as a string) or a missing field, the route will throw a 500 instead of a 422. The client's api.post will then surface a generic error instead of the server's structured error. The compatible alternative is to validate the refresh response with the same PrDetail schema used by the GET route, so a malformed payload is a 422 with a proper error body.

findings.title: Shared contract changed in server copy without the matching client copy
findings.rationale: The diff edits the server copy of contracts/findings.ts (the .nullish() change) but does not make the same edit to client/src/vendor/shared/contracts/findings.ts. Per the house rules, the two copies must change together; otherwise the client silently drifts from the server's contract. This is a warning because the change is safe for callers (a field that becomes nullish instead of optional), but it violates the shared-contract rule.

findings.title: Client's PrDetailHeader now depends on a refresh that may not have run; the GET response no longer guarantees files/commits
findings.rationale: The client adds a Refresh button that calls POST /pulls/:id/refresh, but the GET /pulls/:id response no longer includes files/commits unless a refresh has happened. If a user opens a PR that was never refreshed, the detail page will show empty files/commits until they click Refresh. This is a silent behavior change for the client's own UI and for any external caller that reads those fields from the GET response. The compatible alternative is to have the GET response always include the stored files/commits (even if empty) and document that they are best-effort until a refresh.

Now it returns only the stored subset (number, title, filesCount, etc.) with no files or commits. findings.title: Client refresh mutation throws plain Error instead of ApiError — loses server error code/message
findings.rationale: The new refresh mutation calls api.post<PrDetail>(`/pulls/${prId}/refresh`) and, on a non-2xx response, throws a plain Error. The house rule requires client code that calls the engine to throw ApiError on non-2xx so the page can show the server's message, status, and code. A plain Error loses all of that and shows a generic message. This is a contract violation for the client's error-handling path.

findings.title: Shared contract copies (server and client) not changed in the same diff — they now disagree
findings.rationale: The house rule requires that a change to a shared contract under server/src/vendor/shared/ be mirrored in client/src/vendor/shared/ in the same diff. This PR changes the server route's response shape (GET now returns a subset, POST /refresh returns the full detail) but does not touch either copy of contracts/pulls.ts. The client's type for PrDetail still expects the full detail from GET, so it will silently drift from what the server now returns.

findings.title: GET /pulls/:id no longer backfills filesCount/commitsCount on the Pull Requests list
findings.rationale: The old GET route backfilled filesCount and commitsCount on the Pull Requests list from the detail fetch. The new GET route is a pure read and no longer does this, so the list will show stale or zero counts until a refresh happens. The new refresh route only writes these fields when the detail fetch returns non-empty arrays, so a PR with zero files or commits will never get them updated.

findings.title: New refresh route does not validate PR belongs to repo before fetching from GitHub
findings.rationale: The new POST /pulls/:id/refresh route fetches from GitHub using the PR's number and the repo's owner/name, but does not verify that the PR actually belongs to that repo. A caller who knows a PR ID from a different repo could trigger a refresh on it, potentially leaking data or causing an error. The old GET route validated the repo before fetching.

findings.title: New refresh route does not check token before calling GitHub — will fail with 401/403
findings.rationale: The old GET route skipped the GitHub call when no token was configured, serving cached detail offline. The new refresh route always calls GitHub, so without a token it will fail with a 401/403. The client's refresh mutation will surface this as a generic error (see finding 2), and the page will not show the refreshed data.

The old GET /pulls/:id returned the stored PrDetail shape (camelCase, with files/commits arrays). A client that calls the new endpoint expecting the old detail shape — e.g. the new client mutation `api.post<PrDetail>(...)` — will get a response that does not match the PrDetail type. This is a breaking contract change for any caller that uses the new endpoint.

findings.title: GET /pulls/:id now returns a stored detail that is missing fields the client still reads
findings.rationale: The diff removes the GitHub detail fetch from GET /pulls/:id and instead returns a stored shape built from pr.* fields. The new shape includes number, title, files_count, and a files array with only path, but it drops fields the client still reads from the GET response: files, commits, additions, deletions, changed_files, and the full file objects (additions, deletions, status). The client's PrDetail type and the detail page still expect these. A caller that opens a PR detail page now gets undefined for those fields, breaking the page render and any logic that depends on them. This is a silent behavior change for the existing client.

findings.title: New POST /pulls/:id/refresh returns a different shape than GET /pulls/:id
findings.rationale: The new refresh route returns { ...detail, id: pr.id } where detail comes from gh.getPullRequest. That detail uses GitHub's snake_case fields (files_count, files, commits, additions, deletions, changed_files). The GET route now returns a stored shape with camelCase fields (filesCount, files with only path). The client's PrDetail type and the detail page expect a single consistent shape. The refresh response will have files_count but the GET response has filesCount; the client reads filesCount from the refresh response and gets undefined. This is a contract mismatch between the two routes that the client will hit when the user clicks Refresh.

findings.title: Client refresh mutation throws a plain Error on non-2xx instead of ApiError
findings.rationale: The new mutation calls api.post<PrDetail>(`/pulls/${prId}/refresh`) directly. The house rule states that client code that calls the engine with fetch directly must throw ApiError on non-2xx, not a plain Error, so the page can show the server's message and status. The diff does not show any error handling that converts the response to ApiError. If the refresh fails (e.g., 401, 500), the mutation will throw a plain Error and the page will show a generic message, losing the server's error code and details.

findings.title: Shared contract copies not updated for the new GET response shape
findings.rationale: The GET /pulls/:id response shape changed (removed fields, changed filesCount to files_count, etc.) but neither copy of the shared contract (server/src/vendor/shared/contracts/pulls.ts and client/src/vendor/shared/contracts/pulls.ts) was updated in this diff. findings.title: Deep link is hardcoded rather than derived from a single routing source of truth
findings.rationale: The `reviewUrl` is built by string-concatenating `/repos/${repo.id}/pulls/${r.number}?tab=findings`. If the client's routing ever changes (e.g. the tab param is renamed or the path structure changes), this hardcoded string will silently drift from what the PR detail page actually expects — which is exactly the problem the PR description says it's trying to solve. A more robust approach would be to have the client derive the URL from its own router, or to expose a single shared URL-builder helper. This is a maintainability concern, not a correctness defect today.
